document:
Exercise: Supine One-Arm Overhead Throw

Category:
plyometrics

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- shoulder_extension
- core_engagement

Primary Muscles:

- abdominals

Secondary Muscles:

- chest
- lats
- shoulders

Equipment:

- medicine_ball

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- improve_core_stability_and_strength
- enhance_shoulder_mobility_and_power

Contraindications:

- condition: shoulder instability, reason: risk of injury
- condition: recent shoulder surgery, reason: not recommended until fully healed

Exercise Variations:

- name: Supine One-Arm Overhead Throw to Partner, instructions: ['Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent. Hold the ball with one hand, extending the arm fully behind your head.', 'Throw the ball directly forward of you as you sit up, attempting to go for maximum distance and catch it from a partner.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass, equipment: medicine ball

Instructions:

- Lay on the ground on your back with your knees bent. Hold the ball with one hand, extending the arm fully behind your head. This will be your starting position.
- Initiate the movement at the shoulder, throwing the ball directly forward of you as you sit up, attempting to go for maximum distance.
- The ball can be thrown to a partner or bounced off of a wall.
